They remain tracked in discovered_orgs.json for radar mention-counting and topic-attribution; if mentions resurface via tech_news / blogs / papers, the sweep can re-promote them back to enterprise_vendors. github_collector._comment: Daily GitHub trending + curated watch list. Earlier signal than blogs/news: dev mindshare shows up here first. Scrape github.com/trending (HTML; no auth needed) plus star-count diffs on the watch list. Output: github/{YYYY}/{MM}/{date}.md.
github_collector._watched_comment: These are repos we track star-count delta on every day. Big delta jumps (≥ +500 stars/day) are leading indicators. Manual entries are sacred (no _auto_added flag). The github sweep auto-extends this list per github_sweep_config below.
github_collector._deep_watch_comment: Auto-demoted repos — formerly active in trending, now silent past silence threshold AND watched_repos hit its soft cap. github_stars.json stops tracking these (no daily fetch); they remain in deep_watch_repos for re-promotion if they trend again. Maintained by scripts/run_github_sweep.py. Empty by default.

github_sweep_config._comment: Daily sweep of github/{YYYY}/{MM}/*.md to find repos that consistently trend but aren't yet in watched_repos. Same architecture as vendor_sweep_config and keyword_sweep_config: discovery → sustained-day gate → auto-apply → audit log. Manual entries are sacred; auto-added entries carry _auto_added markers in github_stars.json; deep-watch demotion when watched list hits soft cap.

promotion_thresholds._comment: Repo promoted to watched_repos if it trended on ≥ min_distinct_trending_days within the last rolling_window_days AND has held 'promote' tier for min_consecutive_days_at_promote consecutive sweep runs. Sustained-day gate prevents flash-in-the-pan promotions.

watch_thresholds._comment: Repos with 2 trending days surface in the watch tier of the change log. Not auto-applied.

hot_event_thresholds._comment: A repo with a one-day star delta ≥ this threshold gets a hot-event TTL inclusion (30 days), regardless of trending-day count. Catches viral moments (a single launch that pulls 5k+ stars overnight).

auto_demote._comment: DISABLED for the same reason as vendor + keyword sweeps: a repo going quiet for a few weeks may be in dormancy, not death. Deep-watch is the preferred soft path.

deep_watch_demote._comment: Soft cap on watched_repos with a recency-rank overflow path (parallels enterprise_vendors). TWO regimes: (1) NORMAL — when len(watched_repos) > max_watched_repos, demote _auto_added repos with no trending appearance for >= min_silence_days (30), oldest-silent first. (2) OVERFLOW — when len > max_watched_repos * overflow_factor (> 120), the silence bar drops to overflow_silence_days (14) and the LEAST-RECENTLY-TRENDED _auto_added repos are demoted until len <= ceil(max * overflow_factor) or the per-run budget is spent. Either regime demotes at most max_demotions_per_run per sweep (gradual walk-down, never a mass purge). The repo string is REMOVED from watched_repos and ADDED to deep_watch_repos; its github_stars.json entry gets _demoted_on/_demoted_reason. The github collector skips deep-watch repos for daily star-fetch. Manual entries (no _auto_added in github_stars.json) are NEVER demoted. Repos that trended TODAY are never demoted. Re-promotion happens automatically when a deep-watch repo trends again.

deep_watch_promote._comment: When a repo in deep_watch_repos trends >= 1 time in the rolling window, restore it to watched_repos and refresh its github_stars.json entry. Audit verb: deep-watch-promote.

auto_apply._recovery: sources.json.bak holds the pre-sweep snapshot for rollback. Same single backup file as vendor + keyword sweeps.

hackernews_collector._comment: Daily HN scan. Filter front page + 'new' for AI items by keyword match. HN comment threads on AI launches are often the highest-signal dev sentiment available — surface them. Output: hackernews/{YYYY}/{MM}/{date}.md.
hackernews_collector._min_points_comment: Anything ≥ 30 points + matches a filter keyword is included. Ask HN/Show HN with ≥ 10 points + keyword match also included (lower bar for new launches).

linkedin_collector.comment_priority: topic_over_author — substantive content wins regardless of poster's follower count or title
feeds_to_scan: Pulse search via Google: site:linkedin.com/pulse {topic} (one query per pulse_topic_queries entry, last 14 days)
Pulse search via LinkedIn content search (sortBy=date_posted, datePosted=past-week) for each focus_areas topic
linkedin_collector.url_capture_rule: Captured link must match /pulse/, /posts/, or /feed/update/{urn}. Search-result URLs and bare /feed/ URLs are NOT acceptable — drop the item if you cannot extract a canonical post URL.
linkedin_collector.note: Auto-enabled when Chrome is reachable; silent skip otherwise. Topic-driven Pulse search is the priority layer; hashtag and home-feed scans are secondary.

weekly_digest.output_format: tight summary with links into source dailies

archive_config._comment: Long-tail pruning thresholds for scripts/archive_stale.py. Run periodically (weekly or monthly) to keep discovered_orgs.json and discovered_keywords.json from growing unbounded with single-mention noise. Archives are read-only history; if a slug/phrase resurfaces, the next sweep creates a fresh entry — no auto-restore from archive.

orgs._comment: Org archived if it has <= max_total_mentions AND has been silent for >= min_silence_days. Priority/enterprise/deep_watch orgs are NEVER archived (they're tracked deliberately).

keywords._comment: Keyword archived if it has been judged 'boilerplate' AND the verdict is >= verdict_ttl_days old AND the phrase has been silent for >= min_silence_days. Phrases without a boilerplate verdict are NEVER archived (they're still candidates for promotion).

radar_config._comment: Trend radar — fired daily by orchestrator after daily synthesis. Scores topics by source-weighted convergence over a rolling window; smooths via EMA to avoid daily jumps. Outputs radar/{date}.md (human-read) + radar/{date}.json (structured data for future web app). Tune the constants here; the SKILL reads them at runtime.
radar_config._ema_comment: Two EMAs run in parallel. Fast (α=0.3, ~2.3-day half-life) reacts to news of the day. Slow (α=0.05, ~14-day half-life) tracks structural shifts. Stage classification uses score_slow so loud single events don't bounce topics between stages — fast vs. slow comparison tells you direction. score_fast > score_slow → rising; score_fast < score_slow → fading. Tune 'ema_alpha_slow' lower (e.g., 0.02 → ~35-day half-life) if the radar still feels too event-driven; tune higher (e.g., 0.1 → ~7-day) if it feels too slow to react.

source_weights._comment: Per-mention contribution. Higher = stronger signal. Tune by raising weights for sources you trust more.

convergence_multiplier._comment: When a topic appears in N or more DIFFERENT source types, score is multiplied. Counters monoculture (single-source loud day) and rewards cross-source agreement.

max_mentions_per_source_type._comment: Per-source cap on counted mentions per topic per run. Prevents one chatty source (LinkedIn hashtags, Medium aggregators) from dominating the score just by volume. Beyond the cap, additional mentions are recorded in source_mentions for transparency but stop adding to raw_score. Tune up/down based on what dominates the radar — added 2026-05-12 after LinkedIn accounted for 46% of a topic's score.

clustering_config._comment: Cross-topic clustering — surfaces topics that move together. Built every radar run: for each pair of topics, count days within last 7 where they share ≥1 supporting_file. Topics with co-mention count ≥ min_co_mentions get linked. Connected components → clusters. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: radar treats topics independently, but mcp-adoption + tool-use-standards + a2a-protocol + agent-sdks are clearly one mega-trend.
clustering_config._strategy_comment: After computing connected components, the skill names each cluster with a short 2-4 word label that captures the shared theme. Names are sticky across days (carried forward unless membership shifts > 50%).

velocity_config._comment: Vendor + topic posting cadence acceleration. A vendor whose mention rate triples relative to its 4-week baseline is signalling something. Cheap to compute from data we already have. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'when a vendor's blog cadence accelerates, something's about to ship'.
velocity_config._accelerating_ratio_comment: Velocity_7d / velocity_28d_avg. ≥ 3.0 triggers the 'accelerating' flag. ≥ 5.0 contributes to hot_event tier even without a funding keyword.
velocity_config._decelerating_comment: Below 0.33 (1/3rd of baseline) flags as 'cooling' — informational only, no demote consequence.

stages._comment: Each topic falls into one stage based on score AND sustained signal. Tuning these thresholds shifts how aggressively the radar promotes/demotes themes.

emerging.description: Early signal. 1-2 weak sources or one strong novel source. Worth watching.

consolidating.description: Multiple independent sources are converging on the same take. Pattern is forming.

mainstream.description: Consensus. Most credible sources reference this; further coverage is incremental.

fading._trigger: score declined >25% over rolling window AND was previously >=50
fading.description: Was hot, now declining. Useful to know — don't bet here, expect coverage to dry up.

topic_taxonomy_seed._comment: Seed list of known topics so the radar has stable IDs across days. The group keys (frontier_models, agent_protocols, etc.) are CATEGORY HINTS — they bias initial clustering but are NOT authoritative. Each run's sectors are determined dynamically by the radar skill from the topics that are actually active that week. The field evolves: RAG was a sector once; today its topics scatter across Agents and Retrieval. Agent may add new topic IDs as new themes appear.

sector_config._comment: Dynamic sectors (radar quadrants) — recomputed every run based on what's actually active. Sectors carry over from yesterday's radar unless hysteresis rules trigger a change. This is what makes it a TREND radar (sectors evolve) rather than a fixed taxonomy. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if I had this earlier, we had only Models / RAG, and now from RAG we went to Agents, that's why I say it needs to be flexible.'
sector_config._clustering_method: LLM clusters topics into themes by reading topic labels + supporting context. Prior run's sectors are passed in as starting point — clusterer keeps them when membership is stable, splits/merges/renames only when warranted. The topic_taxonomy_seed group keys above are initial hints, NOT enforced labels.
sector_config._starter_sectors_comment: Used only on the very first radar run when no prior sectors exist. After that, the clusterer evolves them. If sectors get stuck for too long, manually clearing prior_sectors in the most recent radar JSON forces a fresh cluster.

vendor_sweep_config._comment: Daily vendor sweep — runs every day after the radar, NOT just Mondays. Mines discovered_orgs.json (rolling tally) + radar JSONs to classify every org we've seen into: covered & healthy / silent / promotion candidate / hot-event. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'we cover always the same enterprises'. The fixed enterprise_vendors list creates blind spots toward emerging vendors (Cohere, Glean, Sierra, Decagon, Harvey, Asia-region labs, etc.). Sweep surfaces them.

promotion_thresholds._comment: An org becomes a promotion candidate if it crosses ALL of these thresholds AND isn't already on a vendor list.

watch_thresholds._comment: Below promotion, but worth keeping an eye on. Reported in the watch tier.

silence_thresholds._comment: If a vendor IS on a list but their blog URLs haven't yielded a topic-relevant mention in this many days, flag for review.

hot_event_min_thresholds._comment: An org triggers hot-event status when one of its mentions hits a hot keyword. Lower bar than promotion — temporary 30-day inclusion.

vendor_sweep_config._seed_org_list_comment: Bootstrap-time list of ~100 AI companies the extractor knows about. Used by the bootstrap script for keyword matching. Going forward the skill LLM-extracts org slugs from radar JSONs' breadth_orgs_*; the seed list is only the floor.

auto_apply._comment: When enabled, the sweep MUTATES sources.json directly — adds promotions and hot-event inclusions, removes expired ones. The user no longer reviews recommendations. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'i dont want to do that by myself, you need to do that directly.' Promotions are additive (low risk). Demotions are NEVER automatic. Every auto-added entry carries _auto_added/_added_on/_added_reason flags so manual entries are never touched.

auto_promote._comment: Add to enterprise_vendors after the org has sat at 'promote' tier for at least N consecutive sweep runs. Prevents flash promotions from a single noisy day.

auto_hot_event._comment: Funding/M&A/IPO signals trigger immediate inclusion (no consecutive-day wait — the whole point is to react fast). Marked with _expires_on = today + ttl_days. Auto-removed when expired unless promoted to sustained promote tier in the meantime.

auto_demote._comment: DISABLED. Silent vendors get flagged in the change log but stay on the list. Auto-removal is risky (blog URL might just be temporarily 503-ing). To enable: set true; the sweep will remove enterprise_vendors entries that exceed the silence threshold AND have _auto_added: true (manual entries are still preserved). NOTE: deep-watch demotion (see deep_watch_demote below) is a softer, preferred alternative — entries are moved aside rather than deleted, with a re-promotion path.

deep_watch_demote._comment: Soft cap on enterprise_vendors with a recency-rank overflow path so the cap actually converges instead of waiting on an absolute silence window a barely-active vendor evades forever. TWO regimes, evaluated against the post-adds list: (1) NORMAL — when count > max_enterprise_vendors, demote _auto_added entries silent for >= min_silence_days (30), oldest-silent first (last_seen ascending). (2) OVERFLOW — when count > max_enterprise_vendors * overflow_factor (i.e. > 45), the list is badly over cap, so the silence bar drops to overflow_silence_days (14): demote the LEAST-RECENTLY-MENTIONED _auto_added entries (last_seen ascending) until count <= ceil(max * overflow_factor) OR the per-run budget is spent, whichever comes first. Either regime demotes at most max_demotions_per_run per sweep, so convergence is gradual (a 91→30 walk-down takes several runs, never a mass purge). Demoted entries move to news_collector.deep_watch_vendors with _demoted_on / _demoted_reason / _demoted_from='enterprise_vendors'. Manual entries (no _auto_added flag) are NEVER demoted regardless of silence. Entries classified hot_event or sustained-promote TODAY are never demoted (would self-contradict). Hot-event entries within their _expires_on TTL are exempt from overflow demotion (let the TTL expire them instead). The news collector skips deep_watch_vendors entirely — they exist only so the radar can recognize a returning vendor as continuation, not a brand-new promotion. Re-promotion happens automatically when a deep-watch vendor hits hot_event or sustained-promote in a future sweep. Audit verbs: deep-watch-demote, deep-watch-promote (overflow demotions carry reason="overflow: least-recent, N/cap over soft cap").

deep_watch_promote._comment: When a vendor in deep_watch_vendors is classified hot_event OR meets promote thresholds in a sweep, move them back to enterprise_vendors (carry forward original entry fields, drop _demoted_on/_demoted_reason, refresh _added_on, log deep-watch-promote). This closes the loop so a returning vendor doesn't compete with brand-new promotions for soft-cap headroom.

auto_expire._comment: Remove enterprise_vendors entries whose _expires_on < TODAY AND _auto_added: true. Preserves manually-added entries even if they happen to have an expiry field.

auto_apply._recovery: Before each mutation, sources.json is copied to sources.json.bak (overwrites previous backup). To roll back the last sweep's changes: cp sources.json.bak sources.json.

output_format.primary_view: vendor_candidates/{YYYY}/{MM}/{date}.md — human read, sections for promote/watch/silent/hot
output_format.machine_view: discovered_orgs.json — running tally across all runs

breadth_config._comment: Cross-source breadth — orthogonal to the EMA-based persistence score. Answers 'how many distinct organizations are talking about this right now?' as a primary, visible dimension. User-stated reason 2026-05-14: 'if many companies are talking or writing about the same topic, this means high-weighted related, should be seen easier.'
breadth_config._org_definition: An 'org' is an ACTOR in the topic — an organization that shipped/announced it, adopted/deployed it, regulates it, is hiring for it, or is directly and specifically affected by it. NOT a messenger (a publisher reporting the story) and NOT a contrast co-mention (a competitor named only for comparison in a roundup). The radar skill applies the actor test per mention; ambiguous cases are EXCLUDED (breadth should under-count, not inflate). For backfill where org data isn't separately stored, breadth is approximated by distinct (source_type, file_date) pairs in the window.
breadth_config._attribution_comment: Breadth counts ACTORS, not messengers or contrast co-mentions. An org counts toward a topic only when it is the subject acting on the topic. Publishers reporting the story and competitors named only for comparison do NOT count. See ai-trend-radar/SKILL.md §4 'actor test'.
breadth_config._publisher_comment: Slugs here are tech-press / analyst publishers and individual commentators — messengers, excluded from breadth counts but STILL kept in source_mentions for transparency. A publisher slug counts toward breadth ONLY if the publisher is itself the subject (e.g. an NZZ story ABOUT NZZ building RAG).
breadth_config._finance_press_note: Banks (macquarie, bnp, goldman, gvc, etc.) count toward breadth ONLY when they are the actor (deploying / investing / issuing a mandate), never when quoted as analysts in a market-reaction story.

thresholds._comment: Lowered 2026-06-03 from 15/20 alongside BREADTH_PLAN actor-attribution. Removing publishers + contrast co-mentions shrinks every topic's org set, so the old 15/20 floor (set against the inflated distribution) would almost never fire. After the first corrected radar run, read breadth_audit.median_breadth_30d and re-tune: high_breadth_7d ~= top-third of the NEW distribution, very_high ~= top-quartile.

output_format.primary_view: radar.md — human read, narrative with stage groupings
output_format.machine_view: radar.json — structured data for future visualization (Angular / HTML / Streamlit / etc.)

keyword_sweep_config._comment: Auto-extension of keyword lists. Same architecture as vendor_sweep_config — discovery → sustained-day gate → auto-apply to the relevant section of sources.json. Manual entries are sacred; auto-added entries carry _auto_added markers and can be expired/rolled back. Proven entries (long history) become permanent.

auto_demote._comment: DISABLED. Same risk as the vendor side: a phrase going quiet for 2 weeks may be a real trend in dormancy that returns later. Deep-watch (below) is the preferred soft path — it preserves the phrase + metadata for future re-recognition rather than deleting outright.

deep_watch_demote._comment: Soft cap per target list. When len(list) exceeds max_per_list[name] AND _auto_added_meta entries are silent for >= min_silence_days, demote the OLDEST-SILENT first up to max_demotions_per_run. The phrase string is REMOVED from the flat list; its metadata moves from {section}._auto_added_meta to {section}._deep_watch_meta in sources.json. PROVEN entries (in _proven_meta) are NEVER demoted regardless of silence — they're permanent trend anchors. Manual entries (no metadata at all) are also sacred. Re-promotion happens automatically when the phrase resurfaces with promote-tier signal in a future sweep — phrase string returns to the flat list, metadata moves back to _auto_added_meta. Audit verbs: deep-watch-demote, deep-watch-promote, target_section column carries the list name.

deep_watch_promote._comment: When a phrase in {section}._deep_watch_meta classifies as hot_candidate or sustained-promote, restore the phrase string to the flat list and move its metadata back to _auto_added_meta. Original first_seen, total_mentions, etc. are preserved — a returning phrase is recognized as continuation, not new. Log verb: deep-watch-promote.
